chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fadl Abu al-'Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the leftover water of the cat, the sheep, the cow, the camel, the donkey, the horse, the mules, wild animals, and beasts of prey, and I did not leave anything except that I asked him about it.

So he said: There is no problem with it. Until I came to the dog, he said: It is filth, impure; do not perform wudu (ablution) with its leftover water. Pour out that water, and wash it with earth the first time, then with water.

key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog, specifically discussed here regarding impurity rulings
key_terms.بِالتُّرَابِ: with earth; used here for the first cleansing of the vessel
key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water; used after earth in the cleansing process
key_terms.فَضْلِهِ: the leftover water remaining after an animal has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water or a vessel after a dog has licked from it?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام concerning the leftover water of various animals. It states that the leftover water of many animals is unobjectionable, but the dog's leftover water is impure, unsuitable for wudu (ablution), and the vessel must be cleansed first with earth and then with water.
